title: Case study: chat system (WhatsApp)

kcs.statement: Each online user keeps a WebSocket connection to a connection server. A session registry maps user id to server, so a message is routed to the recipient's server and pushed down the open socket.
Message order within a conversation comes from a per-conversation sequence number assigned on write, not from client clocks. Clients sort and detect gaps with it.

Messages are persisted before they are acknowledged to the sender. If the recipient is offline, a push notification is sent and stored messages are synced from the last received sequence number when the recipient reconnects.
Chat history suits a wide-column store partitioned by conversation id and clustered by sequence number. Reading recent messages is then one partition range scan.

problem_ideas: 50M concurrent users at 50K connections per server: how many connection servers are needed?
Alice sends 3 messages and they arrive at Bob's server out of order. Show how sequence numbers fix it.
Bob is offline for 2 days. Walk through the push notification and the sync on reconnect.
A connection server crashes. Explain what happens to its users' registry entries and their reconnects.
Design read receipts as small messages flowing in the reverse direction.
Group chat with 500 members: compare fan-out per member with one shared conversation log.
